text.p: Serbia's parliament met in extraordinary session on Tuesday to consider a special law reinstating opposition gains in local elections last November, witnesses said.
President Slobodan Milosevic's Socialists had annulled opposition victories in 14 towns and cities last November, prompting months of mass protests as well as international criticism.

Parliament is expected to endorse the opposition's election victory. A parliamentary legislative committee had approved a Milosevic-inspired draft law recognising the disputed poll results ahead of the assembly vote.

But sceptical of Milosevic's sincerity, the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition and its student allies plan to keep up their marathon daily demonstrations at least until their mandates are officially verified in about 10 days time.

The U.S. State Department said on Monday that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright had personally urged Milosevic to ensure the disputed election results were reinstated and to open a dialogue with Serbia's political opposition.
In the November 17 elections, the capital Belgrade was among the 14 cities in which the opposition triumphed before the results were annulled.
